key: senior chef at a Chennai mess
name: ch24_chennai_mess_burnt_vadas
alt: A senior mess chef laughs kindly at a young helper holding a tray of burnt vadas, remembering the pot of sambar he once spilled himself.
scene: A wide view inside the busy kitchen of a small Chennai mess before the lunch rush, steel vessels on a long gas range and a wall of hanging ladles behind. On the left stands the new helper, a thin nineteen-year-old in a white vest and checked lungi with a towel over his shoulder, holding a steel tray of a dozen blackened, smoking vadas, his shoulders hunched and eyes down, bracing to be shouted at. Beside him the kadai of oil still sends up wavy heat lines. On the right the senior chef, in his fifties, round belly, grey moustache, white apron and a folded cloth cap, has one hand raised as if he was about to scold, but his face has turned into a warm laugh. Above his head floats a large thought bubble showing his own younger self, thirty years ago, slipping as a huge sambar vessel tips over and spills an orange puddle across the floor. Lower right, a small inset bubble shows the fix: a single vada dropped into the oil first, with small bubbles rising around it, and next to it a tray of golden, perfect vadas with a green tick. Warm morning light from a high window, steam everywhere, the mood relieved rather than tense. Labels: "30 YEARS AGO" on top of the thought bubble, "NEXT BATCH" under the golden tray in the inset.

key: neighbours in a Pune housing society
name: ch24_pune_parking_sorry_first
alt: Two versions of the same parking dispute: blaming first starts a fight, admitting your own bad parking first gets the car moved with a laugh.
scene: A split-panel illustration divided by a thin vertical line, both halves showing the same covered parking bay under a Pune housing society building, early morning, a painted white line on the floor between two numbered spots. In each half a small white hatchback sits across the line, blocking a blue sedan in. Neighbour A is a man in his thirties in a light blue office shirt with a laptop bag and car keys; neighbour B is a man in his forties in a white kurta-pyjama holding a steel tumbler of tea. LEFT panel: A points angrily at the hatchback with a jabbing arm; B scowls and counts off on his fingers, and a speech bubble above B shows three small sketches of A's car parked crookedly, each with a red cross, so the argument is spiralling. RIGHT panel: A holds his palm on his chest in an apology and points with the other hand to a small inset of his own car sitting across the line last week; B is laughing, tea tumbler raised, already walking to his hatchback with keys out, and a curved green arrow shows the car backing off the line to leave room. A small wall clock shows eight. Calm morning light, cool on the left, warmer on the right. Labels: "BLAME FIRST" at the top of the left panel, "SORRY FIRST" at the top of the right panel.

name: ch24_kota_silly_mistakes_notebook
alt: A Kota tuition teacher shows a student her own years-old notebook of the silly mistakes she still makes, and the student starts one of his own.
scene: A medium shot inside a small coaching-class room in Kota, a whiteboard behind covered with algebra and a circled minus sign, rows of plastic chairs, a ceiling fan. At a desk in the centre sits a teenage boy of about sixteen in a grey school t-shirt, a test paper in front of him with several red circles where he dropped minus signs, his pen paused and his expression half embarrassed, half curious. Standing beside him, leaning in, is the tuition teacher, a woman in her forties in a maroon salwar kameez with a dupatta, spectacles and a pencil behind her ear. She holds open a battered, dog-eared notebook with a taped spine. The open page is large and readable: a big minus sign drawn at the top and a column of short dates running down it, "2009", "2015", "2024", each with a small tick, showing years of catching the same slip. She is smiling and pointing at the page with one finger. On the desk near the boy lies a fresh new notebook, which he has just started, with a small minus sign on its first page and a curved arrow from her notebook to his. Bright afternoon classroom light, encouraging mood. Labels: "SILLY MISTAKES" on the cover strip of the teacher's notebook, "MINUS SIGN" on the open page heading.

name: ch24_lucknow_nephew_rescue
alt: A nephew's blunt remark embarrasses his proud uncle, then honest praise of the uncle's real strengths turns his face from red to beaming.
scene: A two-moment illustration divided by a thin vertical line, set in the courtyard of an old Lucknow family house with arches, a jharokha window and potted tulsi. The same two people appear in both halves. The eldest uncle is a heavy man in his sixties in a cream sherwani-style kurta and a Nehru jacket, grey moustache, spectacles; the nephew is a young man of about twenty-five in a jeans and striped shirt, a phone in his pocket. LEFT panel: the nephew has just blurted something, one hand flying to his mouth in alarm, a speech bubble from him with a large red exclamation mark; the uncle stands stiff with arms crossed, his face flushed red with small heat lines, an offended look. RIGHT panel: the nephew stands with open palms, modest and smiling, and a thought bubble beside the uncle shows a big family tree with many little linked circles, the thing the uncle truly knows; the nephew's own side shows only a small phone icon. The uncle is now beaming, his arm around the nephew's shoulders, and two family members in the background (an aunt in a sari, a cousin) look on smiling. Afternoon light through the arches, warm and relieved. Labels: "OOPS" at the top of the left panel, "RIGHT HAND" at the top of the right panel.

key: Mumbai local train at rush hour
name: ch24_mumbai_local_sorry_order
alt: The same two sentences in a crowded Mumbai local, in opposite order: blame first earns a glare, sorry first earns a nod and a little room.
scene: A split-panel illustration divided by a thin vertical line, both halves showing the packed doorway of a Mumbai suburban train at rush hour, yellow grab poles, overhead handles, a crowd of commuters pressed together and a blurred platform outside. In each half a young commuter in his twenties with a backpack worn on the front has just squeezed in and stepped on the foot of a middle-aged man in a grey shirt holding a handle; a small star of impact marks the foot. LEFT panel: the young man's two speech bubbles are numbered, bubble 1 large with an angry pointing finger at the doorway, bubble 2 tiny with "sorry" in small letters; the older man glares with arms folded, a little blue frost cloud above him, and nobody shifts. RIGHT panel: the order is reversed, bubble 1 large with a hand on the heart and "sorry", bubble 2 small with a finger pointing gently at the jammed doorway; the older man nods with a small smile and shuffles aside, a curved green arrow showing a little space opening up next to him. Late evening light through the open door, the left half cool and tense, the right half warmer. Labels: "WRONG ORDER" at the top of the left panel, "RIGHT ORDER" at the top of the right panel.

key: father in Kochi catches his son
name: ch24_kochi_father_confession
alt: A father in Kochi sits beside his teenage son and confesses his own paan masala habit, and the boy throws the gutka packet away himself.
scene: A medium shot on the front verandah of a Kerala house in Kochi, red-oxide floor, a wooden easy chair, coconut palms and a green banana plant beyond the low wall, a school bag lying open on the step. The father, in his forties, wearing a white mundu and a light checked shirt, sits on the verandah step beside his fourteen-year-old son in a white school shirt and navy shorts. The father is not shouting: his hand rests on his own chest and he leans towards the boy, talking quietly, and a large thought bubble above him shows a close-up of a stained, cracked tooth with a small calendar strip beside it marked with four crossed-out attempts to stop. The boy looks at the floor, thinking, and holds a small red gutka packet over a dustbin, his hand opening; a dashed arrow shows the packet dropping into the bin. A small inset bubble at the top right shows the same verandah a year later, the father pushing away a tin of paan masala with a green tick beside it. Soft late-afternoon light, quiet and honest mood, no anger anywhere. Labels: "ME TOO" on top of the father's thought bubble, "A YEAR LATER" over the top-right inset.

key: cricket coach at a district academy
name: ch24_nagpur_coach_square_leg
alt: A cricket coach tells a teenage batsman how he too kept getting out playing across the line, and the boy relaxes and listens to the drill.
scene: A wide shot of a practice net at a district cricket academy in Nagpur, green netting on poles, a dusty run-up, a stack of red balls in a bucket and a few orange cones laid in a straight line toward the bowler's end. On the right the teenage batsman, about fifteen, in whites, pads and a helmet pushed up, leans on his bat and laughs, his shoulders loose. On the left the coach, a fit man in his late forties in a navy academy tracksuit with a whistle and a cap, mimes a straight-bat shot with his own bat, showing the correct line. Above the coach floats a thought bubble with his younger self swinging across the line, stumps flying behind him and a cartoon fielder at square leg catching the ball happily, the coach's old nickname implied. Under the cones, a dashed straight arrow runs from the batting crease to the bowler, showing the straight-line drill, and a small curved red arrow with a cross shows the old across-the-line swing beside it. A calendar sheet in the bubble corner shows a whole season of pages flipped. Bright late-afternoon sun, long shadows, a relaxed, friendly mood. Labels: "SAME MISTAKE" on top of the thought bubble, "THE DRILL" beside the line of cones.
